ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has three D-type flip-flops arranged vertically; each flip-flop has a D input, a Q output, and an inverted Q output, and the three Q outputs are labeled P, Q, and R respectively. The D terminals of the flip-flops are driven by the feedback connections and logic gates in the figure; before the middle stage there is an OR-shaped gate with an inversion bubble at the output, before the bottom stage there is an AND gate, and the three flip-flops share a clock input. Reasoning: The problem states that all flip-flops are reset to 0 at power-on, so the initial output is PQR=000. According to the next-state relationship corresponding to the feedback network in the figure, on consecutive clock edges the following are obtained in sequence: 000 -> 010; 010 -> 011; 011 -> 100; 100 -> 000. At this point it returns to the initial reset state and the cycle ends. The different PQR states appearing in the cycle are 000, 010, 011, 100, a total of 4.

method.method_draft: Starting from the text-given reset state PQR=000, apply the visually extracted next-state equations on successive clock edges: 000 gives 010; 010 gives 011; 011 gives 100; 100 gives 000 again. Stop when the reset state repeats. The distinct PQR outputs in the repeating sequence are 000, 010, 011, and 100, so the counter generates 4 distinct states.
